findings:
🔵 [wdog-untagged-fallback-sleeper] CUT/FOLLOW-UP The no-setsid sleeper is launched as bare `sleep "$secs" &` without the `hetero-wall-watchdog-<tag>` argv0, so the new cmdline gate in `_cancel_worker_watchdog` always skips it and the tag-scoped pkill cannot match it; it is only reaped via the TERM trap on WATCHDOG_PID, and when WATCHDOG_PID is empty it lingers as an idle `sleep` until the deadline. Smallest fix: launch it as `bash -c 'exec -a "hetero-wall-watchdog-'"$tag"'" sleep "$1"' bash "$secs" &` (no setsid needed). Excluded: no signal is ever sent, leak is bounded by the timeout, setsid-less hosts only.
🟡 [wdog-trap-stale-sp] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Pre-existing context line, not touched by this diff: the watchdog subshell trap `kill "${sp:-}"` is still a bare-pid kill that can run after `wait "$sp"` has already reaped the sleeper (parent cancels during the 10s grace loop), same class as the cancel-side finding fixed here. Smallest fix: `sp=""` immediately after `wait "$sp"`. Excluded: needs pid reuse inside the grace window, outside the diff.
🔵 [wdog-cgroup-double-failure-silent] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Cgroup path: if `set -m` did not isolate the systemd-run job (WORKER_FALLBACK_PGID empty) and `systemctl --user kill` also fails transiently, `_watchdog_signal_worker` returns 1, `.fired` is removed and the watchdog exits without bounding the run while the result still reports `timeout_enforced: true`. Smallest fix: retry systemctl once, or fall back to `kill -SIG "-$WORKER_RP"` only when `ps -o pgid= -p "$WORKER_RP"` equals WORKER_RP. Excluded: requires two independent failures; spec item 2 keeps the scope kill primary.
🔵 [test-r8-unconditional-reap] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `assert_r8_detached_reaps_worker_session_descendants` calls `reap_pid` (KILL) on `sleeper`/`sleeperi` after `wait_pid_dead` already proved them dead; only a same-uid pid reuse inside the 8s window could reach another process. Smallest fix: `pid_alive "$sleeper" && reap_pid "$sleeper"`. No pkill/pgrep patterns exist in the new tests; every other kill targets a live test-owned child.
🔵 [pgid-has-live-unused] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `_watchdog_pgid_has_live` is defined, exported via declare -f and covered by tests but never called; `_watchdog_worker_alive` inlines the same ps scan plus the WORKER_RP check. Not a defect (zero behavioural effect); delete it or have `_watchdog_worker_alive` delegate to it in a follow-up.
🔵 [test-assert-eq-arg-order] CUT/FOLLOW-UP Several new assertions pass (expected, actual) to a lib `assert_eq` that reads (actual, expected) (e.g. `assert_eq "false" "$(json_get …)"`), so failure messages read backwards, as visible in the recorded RED headers. Equality is symmetric so verdicts are correct; cosmetic.
